_comment: EVERY CLAIM HERE WAS DRIVEN ON THE CUSTOMER PATH, AND NAMES THE ARTIFACT VERSION IT WAS DRIVEN AGAINST.
check-credential-claims-remeasured.mjs fails when a newer version of that artifact publishes, because
the claim then describes bytes nobody has checked. Re-drive it, then move the version here.
Do not edit a version in this file without re-driving the arm it refers to: the version IS the claim
that someone looked.

A claim with driven_by is REPRODUCED ON TODAY'S BYTES by that script, so its measured_version is history rather than a promise and this check does not grade it. Refusal arms can be driven for free -- no credential, no render, nothing billed -- so they are not attested at all. Claims WITHOUT driven_by need a credential or a device to prove, and there the version field is the claim that a human looked.
HOW TO KNOW YOUR RE-DRIVE IS COMPARABLE. Three controls, answering three different questions.
1. POSITIVE CONTROL — can the instrument see anything at all? Search for a string you know is
present, in the SAME sweep. A zero from a blind instrument looks exactly like a real zero:
ugrep's -l prints nothing for a binary match, and that nearly put a false claim on a page.
2. DIFFERENTIAL — can it see THIS string in THIS artifact shape? Run the same method against the
version that still HAS the property. Needed for any 'X is gone' claim: it proves the absence is
the artifact and not the search.
3. BACK-MEASUREMENT — does your recipe reproduce the number you are about to REPLACE? Run your
method against the OLD artifact and check you get the figure already written down. Needed for
any 'unchanged' or 'superseded' claim. Nobody runs it, because re-deriving a number you already
believe feels like work for nothing — right up until the two recipes disagree, at which point
'unchanged' was two methods agreeing by luck, which is indistinguishable from a property holding.
Landed 2026-09-15 after all three were needed in one night: (1) on the Android AAR, (2) on 0.5.6
vs 0.5.7, (3) on the LGPL symbol count before moving that page from 0.5.6 to 0.5.7.
EVERY CLAIM CARRIES A `route`, AND THE CHECK REFUSES WITHOUT ONE. It names the invocation and code path
actually driven — not the command, the ROUTE. This exists because of a real handoff on 2026-09-15: a lane
reported livekit-server as required for `bithuman run`, with a measured refusal, an exact error string, a
machine name and an exit code. All true. The missing qualifier was WHICH ROUTE REACHES IT — on the published
CLI an expression-2 model is routed away from serve and never meets LiveKit at all. The author had read that
routing line by line and compressed it out at the handoff, because by then it was background to them rather
than news. ★A handoff is where the author's context is richest and the reader's is poorest, and compression
runs the wrong way at exactly that point. This field cannot check that a route is RIGHT. It checks that one
was STATED, which turns omission-by-familiarity into a blank instead of confident prose.

NO credential: exit 77 NOT_SIGNED_IN ('not signed in: run `bithuman login`, or set BITHUMAN_API_SECRET') 8.3 s after the pull, nothing listening on the port; `render` with no credential on the same bytes: exit 77 NOT_SIGNED_IN, no output file. INVENTED secret + BITHUMAN_API_BASE=https://meter-unreachable.invalid/ + BITHUMAN_METER_ENFORCE=1: exit 1 'bithuman serve: sign-in failed: auth required (BE_ERR_NO_AUTH): be_auth_authenticate' in 7.7 s, nothing started, nothing listening. REAL credential (read from a mode-600 file into the environment, never argv) with the REAL API base and the variable unset: 'libessence auth configured (env BITHUMAN_API_SECRET)', sign-in passes, 'embedded livekit-server up', first-run brain venv built (pip: bithuman 2.11.5 + livekit-agents 1.5.12), 'embedded agent-worker brain up', 'bithuman is live: http://127.0.0.1:57073/WISEPUP'; a viewer GET /WISEPUP dispatched the brain and 'POST /launch accepted', the litert render host rendered ('ready 416x720 @20fps', rtf 0.43-0.48) and the meter delivered when the session was ended with Ctrl-C after 30.5 s live: '[selfhost-meter] beat seq=1 served=30.6s product=expression-2 delivered (final)', 'beats delivered=1 failed=0 frames=586'. NOT re-driven on 2.6.26: the REAL-credential + unreachable-meter + ENFORCE=1 sub-arm (the 2.6.23 reading — sign-in passes, 74 frames rendered unacked — is the last measurement; the 2.6.26 release notes name no auth or meter-endpoint change) and macOS arm64 (last driven on 2.6.22).

claims.arms: cli-v2.6.26 published Linux x86_64 tarball (sha256 cd50ab74c5…337eadd4 == the .sha256 sidecar, installed by the tap's install.sh into a fresh HOME), env -i, real credential in the environment (read from a mode-600 file, never argv): `bithuman run wise-pup --host 127.0.0.1 --port 57073` (an Expression 2 identity) REACHES THE SERVE PATH — 'embedded livekit-server up at ws://127.0.0.1:33775' (livekit-server 1.13.7 found on PATH, not in the tarball), first-run brain venv built (pip: bithuman 2.11.5 + livekit-agents 1.5.12), 'embedded agent-worker brain up (agent_name=bithuman)', root page at :57073 answers 200, 'bithuman is live: http://127.0.0.1:57073/WISEPUP'; GET /WISEPUP 303s to /WISEPUP/?roomName=room-WISEPUP-… (200), the launcher dispatches the brain into the room ('launcher dispatched code=WISEPUP') and the brain POSTs /launch ('POST /launch accepted … bring_your_own=true target_size=416x720'); the litert render host comes up ('ready 416x720 @20fps model=combined_litert.tflite', rtf 0.43-0.48 at 41-46 fps) and the idle clip streams whole ('idle wrap: frame 148 -> 0 (clip 149 frames, the authored seam)', wraps 1-3); log says brain 10 times, preview 0 times, viewer 0 times. Startup also prints 'WARNING — default audio_encoder.onnx not found; encoder-less .imx models will fail to load' and Wise Pup loads regardless. Ctrl-C (SIGINT to the foreground process group) 30.5 s after the host's READY: 'shutdown signal received', 'graceful drain', the host prints 'stdin closed — exiting' (no KeyboardInterrupt), 'session cancel signalled; releasing slot', and the host's final beat is delivered 2.1 s after the signal — '[selfhost-meter] beat seq=1 served=30.6s product=expression-2 delivered (final)', 'session x2-litert-… closed — beats delivered=1 failed=0 frames=586 served=30.6s' — the CLI exits 0 in 2.2 s, nothing left running or listening. ★The 2.6.25 fix still holds on 2.6.26: on the 2.6.24 bytes the same Ctrl-C killed the render host on KeyboardInterrupt and delivered NO final beat (sessions of ~47 s and ~27 s billed 0 s); 3 of 3 runs on the release-built 2.6.26 Linux bytes delivered it (served 30.6 s each), and the PUBLISHED 2.6.26 bytes installed from install.bithuman.ai into a fresh HOME delivered served=30.8s, SIGTERM 1 of 1, a session the platform ends 1 of 1. THE NO-ARGUMENT FORM: `bithuman run --host 127.0.0.1 --port <n> --json` on the same bytes, its own fresh HOME and no credential, pulled the byte-identical wise-pup.imx (sha256 d2c70beaa48b…) and exited 77 NOT_SIGNED_IN with no ~/.bithuman/avatars/ written — it resolves the same slug on 2.6.26; its serve route was not re-driven with a credential (2.6.23 measured it identical to the slug form; the 2.6.26 notes say unchanged). macOS not re-driven for this arm on 2.6.26. ★NEW ON 2.6.26: an argv census over every process in the live session’s process group reads 13 processes with the credential on 0 argv AND `--keys` on 0 argv — the embedded livekit-server’s key pair moved off its command line into its environment (LIVEKIT_KEYS), read back from /proc/<pid>/environ while the session was up.
